details:
Last Light is a browser-based lunar landing site navigator that helps users reassess landing options when schedules or mission requirements change. A promising location may offer different conditions at a different arrival time. Our project makes those differences easier to investigate by connecting terrain, sunlight, Earth visibility and estimated battery behaviour in one workspace.

Our prototype focuses on a 5 × 5 km area at Connecting Ridge near the lunar south pole. Users specify an allowed landing window, surface mission duration and mission assumptions. They then select a priority, such as preserving power, maintaining Earth visibility, limiting relocation or minimizing schedule changes. The numerical engine evaluates candidate locations and times, filters them against assessed constraints, and ranks the alternatives according to that priority.

Three NASA resources support this process. NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) topography provides elevation information for terrain assessment and horizon calculations. NASA’s long-term lunar polar illumination and Earth-visibility products help screen candidate locations. NASA/NAIF SPICE provides the Sun and Earth geometry for the requested dates. Comparing those directions with the terrain horizon lets us calculate visibility over time. Panel characteristics, electrical demand and battery assumptions then translate sunlight availability into an estimated energy timeline. Long-term illumination maps support screening; they do not substitute for the date-specific mission calculations.

Users can inspect alternatives through an interactive terrain view, candidate comparisons and synchronized timelines. Moving through time helps explain the relationship between changing visibility and battery behaviour. Evidence and provenance information connect results to their sources and assumptions. An AI-backed assistant provides application guidance, while the implemented numerical engine produces the study calculations.

The main benefit is making mission trade-offs understandable and inspectable. A location with favourable sunlight may offer less Earth visibility, while a different landing time may change the power outlook. Last Light helps users examine these relationships instead of relying on a single ranking without context. Our intended users are students, researchers and early-stage mission analysts. We aim to support education and preliminary investigation, helping users identify alternatives that deserve more detailed analysis.

We developed the interface using React, JavaScript, HTML and CSS with Vite. Three.js supports the browser-based terrain visualization. The backend uses Python and FastAPI, with SPICE and NASA datasets supporting the scientific calculations. Git and GitHub support version control and collaboration. Freestyle hosts the application on a Linux virtual machine, with nginx serving the frontend and forwarding API requests, and systemd managing the backend service. OpenRouter connects the backend to the ERNIE model. Users access the application through a web browser without specialized hardware.

Our creative contribution is connecting location and landing time within an explainable comparison workflow. The application brings established NASA resources into a shared interface where users can follow a candidate from requirements through visibility calculations to estimated power consequences.

We considered data resolution, coordinate consistency, mission timing, power assumptions, computational limits and uncertainty. Our regional search evaluates a bounded set of locations and times, so it does not guarantee a global optimum. Ground bearing strength, small rock hazards, trajectory and descent safety, and complete radio-link performance remain unassessed. We keep these unknowns visible alongside the results.

Future development includes additional verified lunar regions, localization, lighter views for slower connections and queued computation for more simultaneous users. Further validation of AI-assisted planning and possible satellite-relay integration are separate next steps.

We used ChatGPT/Codex and image-generation tools to assist development, debugging, design exploration and documentation. Lovable assisted presentation design. Our team remains responsible for the implementation, interpretation and submitted work.
